newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Dostum warplanes hit Taleban positions - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Dostum warplanes hit Taleban positions - spokesman.

text.p: The Taleban militia is fighting forces allied with the ousted Afghan government along a new front in northwestern Afghanistan, a spokesman for the ousted military chief confirmed on Saturday.

He said the fighting, involving mostly infantry and armoured vehicles, was taking place in Badghis province, which borders the Central Asian republic of Turkmenistan. It is one of six provinces controlled by the Jumbish-i-Milli faction of northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum.

"The fighting in Badghis, according to our information, is around the town of Qala-i-Nau," Doctor Abdullah (one name), the spokesman for Ahmad Shah Masood, told reporters in the town of Jabal Os-Siraj, 70 km (45 miles) north of Kabul.
Abdullah added that warplanes belonging to Dostum had bombed Taleban positions north of Kabul on Saturday morning. "(Dostum) jets from the north went over this morning," he said.

The air attack was confirmed by ousted government troops in Bagram, a few kilometers north of the frontline, who said they saw two warplanes bomb Taleban troops dug in on the strategic De Sabz pass north of Kabul.
"They hit a (Taleban) tank," said one of the fighters.

Dostum was denounced during Friday prayers in the capital Kabul by the radical Islamic Taleban militia, which seized the city at the end of last month placing two thirds of the country under its control.
Abdullah said Masood's Jamiat-i-Islami faction, now allied with Dostum's troops and fighting their way back towards Kabul, was not concerned at the opening of a second front.
"We are not worried, the Taleban can open as many new fronts as it wishes," said Abdullah.
Early on Saturday morning, a Taleban jet attracted scattered anti-aircraft fire above Jabal Os-Siraj, where Masood is headquartered, but there was no word on casualties.
